items: Indexes occupy the buffer pool
A rarely-used index still evicts hot table pages
Too many indexes slows the planner itself
It must cost more candidate paths every parse
Boolean or 3-value status indexes: planner seq scans anyway
(a) is fully subsumed by (a, b) — drop the narrow one
Duplicates under different names cost writes, buy nothing
Random-UUID PKs split pages across the whole tree
Use UUIDv7, ULID, or a sequence instead
A naive CREATE INDEX takes a write lock
Use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, or an online DDL tool
Slower, and can leave an INVALID index if it fails
Bulk load: drop indexes, load, rebuild — often far faster

blocks.title: Ratio Heuristic
blocks.text: On a write-heavy OLTP table, get suspicious past ~5 indexes. Justify each one with a real query.

items: `WHERE price * 1.2 > 100` — move the math right-hand side
varchar column compared to an integer literal: full scan
int vs bigint in MySQL casts implicitly and kills the index
`LIKE '%term'` cannot seek — leading wildcard
Real suffix search needs a pg_trgm trigram index
Case-insensitive needs citext or an expression index
OR across different columns defeats a composite index
Rewrite as UNION ALL, or lean on a bitmap OR
`NOT IN` and `<>` are unselective — seq scan is correct

blocks.title: Verify In Production
blocks.text: 'It exists locally' is not evidence. Check with \d table or SHOW INDEX FROM table, and re-check idx_scan a week later.

items: `LIKE '%term'` cannot seek — no prefix to descend on
Use a pg_trgm trigram index for infix search
Or a reversed-column index if you truly need suffixes
Case-insensitive search needs citext or an expression index
A collation-aware index works too — a plain one does not
OR across different columns defeats a composite index
Rewrite as UNION ALL, or lean on a bitmap OR of two indexes
`NOT IN` and `<>` are unselective — seq scan is correct
`WHERE b = ?` on index (a, b) skips the leading column
That index can only be fully scanned, if used at all

blocks.title: Sort Direction Counts
blocks.text: ORDER BY a ASC, b ASC cannot use an index on (a ASC, b DESC). Only that exact order and its full reverse are free.

Check idx_scan a week later to prove it gets used

blocks.title: One Line
blocks.text: Fix the statistics before you add the index, and fix the query before you force the plan.

caption.text: Part 2 of SQL INDEXES & QUERY PLANS. Your index exists, it is on the right column, and the planner still refuses to touch it. That is not a bug — it is cost estimation doing exactly what you told it to. 10 pages on B+tree internals, composite column order, covering indexes, reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE line by line, and the ten ways a query silently disables the index you already built.
